sources.entry: Spectacle - Spectacle allows you to organize your windows without using a mouse.

summary.one_liner: Spectacle is a macOS app for organizing windows (moving and resizing them to screen regions) using keyboard shortcuts instead of a mouse; the author says it is no longer actively maintained.
summary.what_it_does: Spectacle assigns keyboard shortcuts to window actions that move or resize the focused window. Actions include centering, maximizing, snapping to the left, right, top or bottom half, snapping to the four corners, and cycling through thirds of the screen. It can also grow or shrink windows, move windows to the next or previous display, and undo or redo window moves with a history. The default shortcuts can be remapped or cleared. The README says Spectacle uses Apple's Accessibility features and must be granted access to them.
use_cases: Snap windows to halves or corners with the keyboard
Organize windows on a Mac without a mouse
Move windows between multiple displays with shortcuts
Undo and redo window position changes
Resize windows in thirds of the screen
how_to_run: Press Command+R in Xcode to run Spectacle
Or download a prebuilt release from the project's download links (version 0.8.6 for Mac OS X 10.7, newer releases need 10.9 or later)
stack: Objective-C/Swift (Xcode project, not specified in README)
notable: Keyboard-driven window snapping to halves, quarters and thirds
Repeated shortcut presses cycle a window between 1/3, 2/3 and 1/2 sizes
Window action history with undo and redo shortcuts
caveats: Not actively maintained; the author recommends Rectangle as an alternative
Newer releases only support macOS 10.9 or greater
Some apps, such as Terminal, or windows with minimum size constraints may not resize exactly as expected
keywords: snap window to half of screen
